name: Metabase
description: Open source business intelligence and analytics platform. Create dashboards and explore data without writing SQL.
summary: Metabase is actively releasing frequent patch updates across multiple supported branches simultaneously. The latest release is v0.63.2 (Open Source) / v1.63.2 (Enterprise), released on July 29, 2025. Multiple older branches (58.x through 62.x) are also receiving concurrent patch updates, indicating strong long-term support policies. Full changelogs are available at https://github.com/metabase/metabase/releases but individual release notes in the scraped content are sparse, linking only to 'Full Changelog' diffs.

answers.What is the current license?: Open Source edition uses AGPL v3; Enterprise edition uses a commercial license
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases across several branches on July 28–29, 2025, with 48.6k GitHub stars
answers.Is there a cloud-hosted version availabl: Yes — Metabase Cloud (managed cloud) is available at metabase.com
answers.Does it support SSO and SAML authenticat: Yes — SSO and SAML are supported in the Enterprise edition
answers.What databases/data sources are supporte: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite, MongoDB, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Presto, Druid, Oracle, Vertica, SparkSQL, and more via drivers

alternatives.name: Redash
alternatives.review: Open source, query-focused, simpler feature set.

alternatives.name: Apache Superset
alternatives.review: Apache-licensed, rich visualisation library, steeper setup curve.

alternatives.name: Grafana
alternatives.review: Primarily metrics/time-series but increasingly used for general BI.

alternatives.name: Hex
alternatives.review: Close source, enterprise focus, AI Analytics Platform for your whole team

alternatives.name: Tableau
alternatives.review: Tableau offers superior data visualization depth and enterprise features but is proprietary, expensive, and not self-hostable in an open-source sense.

alternatives.name: Lightdash
alternatives.review: Lightdash is open-source and integrates tightly with dbt for a metrics-layer approach, but has a narrower ecosystem and smaller community compared to Metabase.
